clue.text: Employing periodic French Polish master

indicators.note: employing these words means putting their letters to use in a new order, the anagram signal here

explanation.surface: Someone uses a recurring French influence, like a Polish master who worked in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employing' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of PERIODIC FRENCH are used to make the name. Fittingly, the composer was half French and settled in Paris, and his first name is in its French form.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic composer of nocturnes and mazurkas was born in Poland and is its most celebrated musical master.

clue.text: Review European clubs into hip-hop?

indicators.note: into places the two letters inside the music genre

parts.note: rap is the vocal style of hip-hop
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether European clubs have taken up hip-hop music.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise the main points again is a short form of recapitulate, a synonym of reviewing them.

clue.text: Bouclé woven into ideal Jersey product

indicators.note: into sends the rearranged fabric letters inside the word for ideal

parts.note: a dream is an ideal

indicators.note: woven means interlaced, so the letters of the fabric are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Bouclé yarn woven into an ideal Jersey knitwear garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey here is the Channel Island, famous for its dairy cattle, not the knitted sweater; 'woven' scrambles the fabric's letters, which split DREAM after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey cows give rich milk, and the thick high-fat dairy topping is a famous product of the island.

clue.text: Check holiday weather — not ideal for sunbathing

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
rain is weather that spoils sunbathing

explanation.surface: Someone checks the holiday forecast and finds it poor for sunbathing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back or curb something is to keep it in check, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Weird nerd from central French city

indicators.note: weird means strange, signalling these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd geek comes from the middle of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' belongs to the anagram fodder, though it seems to describe the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in the Auvergne in central France is home to Michelin tyres.

clue.text: See 1
Reluctant to intervene in company's Fate?

indicators.note: the word for reluctant comes between the letters of the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company; the apostrophe s is a link
loth means reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to interfere in their firm's destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the three Fates spun, measured and cut the thread of life; this one spun it.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest of the three Moirai of Greek myth spun the thread of each mortal life.

clue.text: Grampus regularly leaving no trace

indicators.note: regularly leaving means every other letter is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A whale swims off without leaving a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Grampus is an old name for the killer whale, also called the orc or orca.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale, once called a grampus, is also known by this older word for an orca.

clue.text: Badmouth American hiding golden fleece?

indicators.note: the slur takes the abbreviation inside it, hiding it from view

parts.note: to insult is to badmouth
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone slanders an American who is concealing the mythical Golden Fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a fleece keeps warmth in. 'Golden fleece' looks like Jason's prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece jacket keeps body heat from escaping, so it is an example of a material that blocks heat loss.

clue.text: Brushes off Cristiano Ronaldo, initially relegated to the bench?

indicators.note: the footballer's initials are sent into the word for the substitutes, as a player is sent to sit among them

parts.note: the bench is where the substitutes, or subs, sit

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the footballer's names

explanation.surface: A football manager dismisses a star player by dropping him to the substitutes' bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush something off a surface is to clean it by rubbing, a synonym of scouring it with a brush.

clue.text: He hopes to relieve people of their unwanted possessions

definitions.text: He hopes to relieve people of their unwanted possessions

parts.words: He hopes to relieve people of their unwanted possessions
parts.note: the surface suggests a house clearer taking away junk; the possessions are demonic possessions

explanation.definitionFit: A priest who casts out demons frees people from being possessed by evil spirits, the second sense of possessions.

clue.text: Ordinary soft aluminium, hydrated silica

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A list of materials: plain soft metal and silica with water bound in.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemstone is mineralogically a form of amorphous silica containing water, so a chemist's description of it.

clue.text: Dilapidated hut located in exotic realm

indicators.note: the hut is set inside the rearranged letters, as a building is located in a region
exotic means strange or foreign, signalling the letters of realm are rearranged

parts.note: a shack is a crude hut

explanation.surface: A tumbledown cabin sits in some faraway foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the letters of 'realm', and the hut sits after their first three.
explanation.definitionFit: Something falling to pieces from neglect is described with this synonym for tumbledown or rickety.

clue.text: "Tea, Monsieur?" Foreign capital welcoming a PM in crisis

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: the city takes in the letter, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: Berlin is the German capital

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is offered tea while a foreign capital hosts a prime minister in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain was the British prime minister during the 1938 Munich crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain led Britain through the Munich appeasement crisis of 1938 as its premier.

clue.text: Musk receiving shock therapy (current choice)

indicators.note: the tycoon's first name takes in the other letters, as a host receives guests

parts.note: Elon Musk, the tech billionaire
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A tech billionaire undergoes electric shock treatment, with a pun on current.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis hides that 'current' is the physics symbol I, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters make a choice between candidates at a poll, so the ballot itself is a formal choosing.

clue.text: He takes an arm and a leg, like one who terrorised Amity Island, reportedly

definitions.text: He takes an arm and a leg

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: lone means single, one alone; Amity Island is the town in Jaws, terrorised by a great white

explanation.surface: A predator takes limbs, like the creature that terrorised Amity Island in Jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An arm and a leg' is an idiom for an exorbitant price, so the definition is a usurer, not a man-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortionate moneylender charges crippling interest, the idiom for costing an arm and a leg.

clue.text: Nothing following gold tesla car

indicators.note: following places the zero after the other pieces

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Reads as a gold Tesla car with nothing coming after it.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-less 'tesla' is the physics unit, not the car brand that the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An automobile is shortened to this word, still used for a car in American and European speech.

clue.text: Bilk allegedly boring, horrible kid's game of cards

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the sound-alike goes inside the word for a nasty child

parts.note: a brat is a horrible child

indicators.note: allegedly means as said rather than spelt

parts.note: Acker Bilk was a British jazz clarinettist

explanation.surface: Someone claims a bilker is boring and plays cards with a horrid kid.
explanation.walkthrough: Acker Bilk was a British clarinettist famous for Stranger on the Shore; his first name gives ACKER, said as ACCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino card game of punto banco type is associated with James Bond.

clue.text: Ball caught out Schmeichel, for one

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is taken out of the word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper drops a ball and the batsman is caught out, mixing football and cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Schmeichel was Denmark's famous goalkeeper, and 'Ball' is a dance, not a football.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmeichel is a native of Denmark, so he is an example of a person of that nationality.

clue.text: French writer's cab getting puncture outside

indicators.note: outside puts the word for a puncture around the cab firm

parts.note: a flat is a punctured tyre
Uber is the ride-hailing cab company

explanation.surface: A French author's taxi suffers a puncture on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'writer's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Madame Bovary is a nineteenth-century novelist from France.

clue.text: Huge flood of water to carry in river

indicators.note: in says the carrying word goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A vast flood brings water to be carried into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrential downpour or overwhelming inundation is described by this word, as in Noah's great flood.

clue.text: Like sports bars, mister? YMCA rocks!

indicators.note: rocks means shakes up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone cheers about gym equipment at the YMCA, saying it rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Uneven bars in women's gymnastics are also called asymmetric bars, so the sports bars are gym apparatus, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The gymnastics apparatus has two rails at unequal heights, lacking symmetry, hence its other name.

clue.text: Baby food making its way into mouth in Newport?

definitions.text: Baby food making its way into mouth in Newport?

parts.words: Baby food making its way into mouth in Newport?
parts.note: a teething biscuit heads for an infant's mouth, while the question mark hints at the Welsh river that reaches the sea at Newport

explanation.walkthrough: Newport is a city in south Wales at the estuary of a river whose name, after an R, completes the biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard dry biscuit given to teething infants is a classic first solid food for babies.

clue.text: Fast network cut in street

indicators.note: in places the shortened network inside the street abbreviation
cut means the end is lopped off the word

parts.note: wifi is a wireless network

explanation.surface: A speedy network gets cut off out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the last letter off WIFI, leaving WIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick or rapid movement is described by this adjective, a straightforward synonym of speedy.

clue.text: Did he come after Julius riding a noble steed?

definitions.text: Did he come after Julius riding a noble steed?

parts.words: Did he come after Julius riding a noble steed?
parts.note: the Roman emperor followed Julius Caesar's line and supposedly planned to make his horse a consul

explanation.walkthrough: Julius is also the setter's name. The emperor was said to want his horse Incitatus made a consul, a noble steed indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious Roman emperor ruled after Julius Caesar's dynasty began and doted on his favourite horse.

clue.text: Rogue wife abandoning sissy

indicators.note: abandoning means the word for sissy is left without the wife's letter

parts.note: a wimp is a sissy

explanation.surface: A rogue walks out on his wife and a sissy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous little devil or rascal is a mild rogue, a playful synonym.

clue.text: Every now and again, Rio van driver transports crew member

indicators.note: every now and again means take letters at intervals, here the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A van driver in Rio carries a member of the band's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring band's road crew includes technicians who shift and set up equipment, each one a member.

clue.text: English magistrate approves returning capital

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read from back to front

parts.note: a JP is a Justice of the Peace, a magistrate
OKs means approves

explanation.surface: An English magistrate approves someone's return.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of North Macedonia, so a national capital.

clue.text: Expected Eton at eleven. About to set off

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the words around contain the letters needed

explanation.surface: A boy is due at Eton College at eleven and is about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to set off' reads as one phrase, but 'About' signals the hidden word and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to explode it, so the verb means to make a charge go bang.
